internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: volitional refusal: holding oneself back from accepting or performing what is presented or required
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All 13 occurrences describe refusing, declining, or insisting against an offered/commanded course. Ability and outcome vary; the subject's withholding of assent/action remains.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Complements identify refused action, and conjunctions may add arrogance or insistence. These attitudes intensify but do not constitute the root.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: Heaven and earth 'refuse' the trust in 33:72, extending volitional language to cosmic participants; the verse still contrasts acceptance with withholding.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The core is arrogance; refusal without explicit arrogance and coordination 'refused and was arrogant' separate the two.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from inability, which lacks volitional withholding, and from disobedience, which can occur after assent.
internal_discovery.rationale: Volitional withholding is explicit and contrastively bounded in every occurrence.
